list: The official 55 PlayStation 5 trophies, as Exophase and PSNProfiles listed them on 18-19 Nov 2026. Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's own words; the guides beside them are this entry's own words.
note: Grand Theft Auto VI released on 19 Nov 2026, the day this guide was written. No full verified walkthrough exists yet. Where a guide gives a specific place or step, it names its source; where no source has confirmed a method, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing one.

psnprofiles.label: PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophies (PSN progress counts)

trophies.guide: The last trophy you earn: it pops on its own the moment the other 54 are done, so there is nothing to do for it directly. Work the roadmap in order — story first, then side stories, activities, robberies and the money grind — and do the one early thing that matters, the Chapter 1 balcony meditation for Positive Mental Attitude, before Chapter 1 ends. Expect a long hunt: first-day estimates put the platinum at around 200 hours.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission. This is the first story trophy and it pops as you play — nothing to prepare and nothing to miss. Hidden on PlayStation until you earn it, so it stays behind the spoiler cover in this guide until then.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1. It pops when the chapter ends, so just play through. Before the chapter ends, do the one thing in it that can be missed: Lucia's balcony meditation for Positive Mental Attitude. The game has no mission replay, so keep a manual save from the start of each chapter.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. It pops when the chapter ends. Character switching between Jason and Lucia opens up during this chapter, which also opens the partner trophies — Hot Together and Retail Therapy need your partner beside you. Keep a manual save from the start of the chapter: there is no mission replay.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. It pops when the chapter ends. Watch for the time-sensitive race in Yago's street racing strand while you are in this chapter — it carries an hourglass icon, and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks. Save before you race it.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4. It pops when the chapter ends. The bank vault robberies for Maximum Withdrawal open near the end of this chapter through the optional mission That's Where The Money Is, so do that mission before you move on to the finale.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final mission. This is the story's gold trophy and it pops with the credits. Before you start the finale, keep an untouched manual save: with no mission replay and no New Game Plus, that save is your way back if you left side content unfinished. Everything outside the story stays available after the credits.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Finish the mission Breakfast Run. It pops when the mission ends, as part of the story. There is no mission replay, so the only way to miss a story trophy is to stop playing the story — play the missions in order and they all come.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Finish the mission The Cartel Heist. It pops when the mission ends. Heist missions are story beats, so this one comes to you — the planning and the robbery trophies in the open world are separate, and they open up later.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Finish the mission Child's Play. It pops when the mission ends. Like the other named-mission trophies, it is a story beat: play the missions in order and it arrives on its own.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Finish the mission Headliners. It pops when the mission ends. The name is a story spoiler, which is why PlayStation hides this trophy until you earn it — the spoiler setting in this guide hides it the same way.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Finish the mission VCIA Takedown. It pops when the mission ends. The airport, VCIA, matters twice: this story mission, and later the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can, where you take a plane from a boarding bridge yourself.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Finish the mission Operation Savage Glory. It pops when the mission ends — the last of the named-mission story trophies before the finale. Once the story is done, the side stories, activities and open-world trophies are all still open to you.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion. This is the hard gold: the checklist itself only appears after the story, under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion, but work you did earlier still counts. The checklist asks for more than the trophies do — 300 stunts instead of 250, 70 of 80 Challenges, 200 of 277 vehicle models and all 39 illegal operations — so use the in-game checklist as your final to-do list once it appears. No difficulty trophies and no mission medals stand in the way; it is long, not hard.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunt jumps, under-the-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps all count, so mix them rather than grinding one kind. Keep going past 250 if you want the platinum: 100% completion needs 300 stunts. PSN tracks your count toward 250.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. PSN tracks 0 of 9. You only need one go at each — a fishing challenge, an arcade game, a drone race, a shooting range challenge, a race, a meditation spot and the rest of the activity list — so sample everything early and the trophy pops while you explore. The 9 types are the game's activity menu; the count on PSN tells you how many you have tried.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN tracks 0 of 42, spread across two shooting ranges. Gold on every challenge is a skill check, not a grind: learn each challenge's scoring, replay the ones you miss, and leave this for a session of its own rather than squeezing it between missions. The silver grade marks it as one of the harder skill trophies.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations — PSN tracks 0 of 14, and you need at least one win per location, not every race. Learn each course's line first with a practice run, then race to win; a location is done once you have won there, so tick them off one by one.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — PSN tracks 0 of 20, and 'different' is the key word: the same race twice counts once. Work through the race list across Leonida, including street races and the Top Fun drone races, and keep a note of which you have won. The Yago street racing strand in Chapter 3 is time-sensitive, so race it the moment it appears.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the 9 activity types, so this also feeds Master of None. Take the challenge when Cal offers it and fish it like any other fishing challenge — steady reeling beats rushing — and if you lose, challenge him again: fishing challenges can be retried.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish it, not just start it. Arcade games are one of the 9 activity types, so this also feeds Master of None. Pick the shortest arcade game you find and play it through to its end screen.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Andy is one of the side characters with his own mission strand; play his missions through to the last one. Side-story finales stay open after the main story ends, so there is no rush — but Andy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, which has its own trophies, so don't expect double credit.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Play Kenton's strand through to its last mission. Like the other side-character finales, it stays open after the main story, so finish it whenever you like — but keep it in mind for the roadmap's side-story stage, since these five finales are easy to leave behind.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Play Billy's strand through to its last mission. Billy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks — only some stranger questlines do — so treat this trophy as its own job, not progress toward the silver.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers — PSN tracks 0 of 8. Only some optional questlines count: Andy's, Billy's and Tyrone's strands do not, because they have their own trophies, so check the trophy's progress counter after each strand you finish. One strand is time-sensitive: the Chapter 3 race against Yago carries an hourglass icon, so save first and race it the moment it appears, or that strand may be lost.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. Play Randy's strand through to its last mission. Side-story finales stay open after the main story, so this is a cleanup trophy for the side-story stage rather than a race against the story.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Play Tyrone's strand through to its last mission. Tyrone's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, so finish it for its own sake and check the Strangers & Freaks counter separately after your other strands.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots — PSN tracks 0 of 18. Meditation spots show as purple icons when you are close. Bring your partner every time: each outdoor spot should count twice if you meditate there with both characters. The missable one is Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1: after Lucia is home, check the kitchen in the morning — a morning after the mission Down to Earth is the usual time — and follow her out to the balcony of Jason's house to accept the optional task. It is gone once Chapter 1 ends, so do it then and keep a Chapter 1 save until the trophy pops. It is not confirmed that the trophy strictly needs that spot, so do it anyway.
trophies.missable_note: The one trophy first-day guides flag as missable: Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1 disappears after that chapter, and the game has no mission replay.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret Vogel's hunting questline is Jason-only and sends you after animals through target decks. Take a clean head or heart shot to keep the carcass pristine. Hidden on PlayStation until earned, so the spoiler setting hides it here until you tick it off.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — PSN tracks 0 of 3. Cards are a pure collectible grind: pick them up as you explore Leonida and the sets complete over time. No confirmed card map exists yet on launch day, so sweep each area as you pass through it rather than hunting blind, and check your set progress in the game's collectibles screen.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — PSN tracks 0 of 100. WAiNK is the in-game app you use to scan and tag things; use it everywhere you go, a little at a time, and the count climbs without a dedicated grind. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app also counts as discovering it for Whip It Good, so scan traffic as you drive and feed both trophies at once.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges — PSN tracks 0 of 50. Challenges are listed under Progress, then Challenges, and many complete on their own while you play. Keep going past 50 if you want the platinum: 100% completion needs 70 of the 80 Challenges. Check the list after each session and pick off the ones nearest done.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. The easiest way is a bank vault job: vaults give you a 4-star Wanted Level straight away, and escaping one with your partner earns this at the same time. It only pops once you have left the red heat zone, not just the flashing search area, so keep driving until the heat is fully gone.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. Call your partner first, then rob three shops in a row while the police are still chasing you. If the stars fade and you are only in the red heat zone, the chain breaks — so keep the heat alive between shops. The trophy can take about 30 seconds to pop after you leave the third shop, so give it a moment before you hit a fourth.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — PSN tracks 0 of 100. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app counts as discovering it, so scan traffic as you drive instead of only counting cars you have driven. Keep going past 100 for the platinum: 100% completion needs 200 of the 277 base models.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aim — press L3 and R3 while aiming. Pick a group of gang enemies, such as the guards at an illegal operation, and use an assault rifle so you can chain the kills inside one Focus. Adrenaline extends Focus, so build it first.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport. Steal a large passenger plane that is docked at a boarding bridge; planes parked elsewhere on the airfield do not count. The planes at gates E3 and E4 work. Go up to the cockpit, back out toward the runway and take off. The trophy is delayed: fly about 1 km away from the airport and it pops. Save first, because the police come fast.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Get into a Rhino military tank — that is what 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' means. Tanks should be parked on the south side of Mile Zero Air Station, on the island at the far southwest of the map. Save first, get in, and drive and fire until it pops. Expect heavy police attention the moment you take one.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. The Chapter 3 mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry store robberies. Go to a store's locked back door and use the Snap Gun on it — kicking the door in sets off the alarm. Inside the back room, find the note with the safe code, open the safe, and leave without being seen. Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City is a good target. If someone spots you, reload rather than push on.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — PSN tracks 0 of 5. Bank vaults unlock through That's Where The Money Is, an optional mission near the end of Chapter 4. Tail an armored security van to a large bank and get into the vault while the guard has it open. You cannot carry all the bags alone, so bring your partner. Each vault job gives you a 4-star Wanted Level straight away, so escaping with your partner also earns Hot Together. The 100% checklist needs all eight vaults, so keep going past five.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Find an armored truck on the road, stop it, take its cargo and get away. Like Hot Together, it only pops once you have left the red heat zone, not just the flashing search area — so keep moving until the heat is fully gone before you relax.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — PSN tracks 0 of 52. This is a map-completion trophy: visit every named area on the map. It fills in naturally if you travel for the other open-world trophies, but check the map for areas you have never entered and sweep them deliberately at the end. Nothing here is missable; everywhere stays open after the story.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — PSN tracks 0 of 9. One per gang is enough for the trophy, so spread your robberies across all nine gangs instead of hitting the same gang's spots twice. The 100% checklist wants all 39 operations, so this pops along the way to that bigger grind.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. No verified method has been published yet — the game released today, 19 Nov 2026, and first-day guides list this as one of the trophies with no confirmed trigger. What the official description asks is plain: find a bar on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and enjoy the view. Try it once the area is open to you and tick it off when it pops; do not trust any specific bar name until a guide confirms it.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. No verified method has been published yet — first-day guides list this as one of the trophies with no confirmed trigger. The description points at a showroom smash-out, in the style of the series' classic moments, so look for a vehicle showroom you can drive through and out of. Until a guide confirms the exact spot, treat any named showroom as unconfirmed.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The alley is Kingpin Bowling, an illegal operation you visit in Chapter 2. Bring Sticky Bombs and take all three key valuables: the luxury watch in an office, the shotgun on a table, and the contents of the office safe, which you blow open with a Sticky Bomb. Then escape the police. If you leave something behind, the operation comes back later, so it is not missable.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Raise both Jason's and Lucia's Strength attributes to maximum — that is the 'partnership with mass appeal' the description hints at. Buy a gym membership and train with your partner there, since the partner trains alongside you. It should pop when both characters reach maximum Strength. First-day guides report this as the likely trigger; it is not yet independently confirmed.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make 500 choices that change your Criminal Profile — PSN tracks 0 of 500. Robberies and fights feed it, so it fills up without a separate grind if you play the game fully. Keep an eye on the counter; if it stalls late, pick fights and robberies deliberately rather than playing quietly.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. No verified method has been published yet — first-day guides list this as a hidden trophy with no confirmed trigger, and one guide calls it a story trophy that unlocks during the campaign. The name suggests succeeding on a second attempt at something, so play through the story and retry anything you fail; do not chase a specific trick until a guide confirms one.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Experience something strange — the description, 'What the hell just happened?', is deliberately vague. No verified trigger has been published yet; first-day guides list it among the hidden trophies with no confirmed unlock method. It reads like a one-off world encounter, so explore Leonida widely, poke at odd things, and let it come to you rather than hunting a named spot that no source has confirmed.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by — knock a target down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. No verified conditions have been published yet; first-day guides say the precise conditions remain under investigation. Try it on a lone pedestrian from a slow-moving car with a melee weapon, and expect to experiment: the trigger is not yet pinned down.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — PSN tracks 0 of 250,000, and the total is cumulative. Marked bills come from bank and payday loan jobs; launder them by selling them to your contacts. Bank vault jobs are the richest source, so this trophy grows alongside Maximum Withdrawal.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — PSN tracks 0 of 100,000, cumulative across every kind of shop. Buy the things you need anyway — weapons, clothes, car upgrades — and the total climbs. Late in the game, if you are short, buy big-ticket items you actually want rather than throwing money at the cheapest thing.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — PSN tracks 0 of 8. Buy them in the Vice City Real Estate app, which unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver. Together they cost about $160,000, so save for them. Garages the story gives you do not count — only the ones you buy.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — PSN tracks 0 of 10. The Chapter 2 mission Moses opens the Scooter Bros app: take a stolen car to Moses, choose Respray, then Register. From Chapter 3 you can also register cars with a standard tracker at Pay 'n' Spray. Each car needs a free garage space, so buy garages first (Little Boxes) and register cheap cars.
trophies.name: On the Spot
